extracted.intended_audience: Christian laypeople, especially parents, masters, apprentices, and young men
extracted.subtask_description: Didactic Christian dialogue warning young men (esp. apprentices) about vices — drunkenness, theft, and uncleanness — describing their effects and giving practical counsel to parents, masters, and youths. Includes illustrative stories, scriptural citations, and behavioural prescriptions (avoid places/people, choose good households, watch servants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drunkenness: impoverishment
rubrics_metrics.description: It greatly tendeth to impoverish and beggar a man; 'The Drunkard, says Solomon, shall come to poverty.' Many that began with plenty have gone out of it in rags through drunkenness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid habitual drinking; recognise the financial cost of the 'beastly' sin and its tendency to ruin families and inheritances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drunkenness: bodily disease and shortened life
rubrics_metrics.description: Drunkenness brings upon the body many great and incurable diseases so that men come to their end; by drunkenness men often shorten their days and may 'break their Necks' going home drunk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider physical health and longevity as reasons to abstain; note medical consequences are treated as manifest and numerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drunkenness: attendant evils and spiritual stupor
rubrics_metrics.description: Drunkenness is attended with abundance of other evils (woe, sorrow, contention, wounds, redness of the eyes) and 'so stupifies and besotts the soul' that an old drunkard is hardly ever recovered to God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See drunkenness as morally contagious and spiritually dangerous; avoid because it impairs conscience and prevents conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drunkenness: leads to theft and dependence on others' money
rubrics_metrics.description: Those addicted to drink must have money, 'either of his Fathers, Mothers, Masters, or at the high-way'; Young Badman learned to pilfer, sell master's goods, take from the cashbox, and convey wares away to fund his drinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise that drunkenness often causes theft and ruin of employers/families; masters should guard their shops and accounts and be cautious whom they employ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sins are linked ('sins go not alone')
rubrics_metrics.description: Sins go not alone, but follow one the other as do the links of a Chain; one vice (e.g., drunkenness) commonly leads to others (theft, whoredom, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat early vices seriously because they tend to propagate further wickedness; intervene early in apprenticeships/households.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master's duty: be wary whom you keep as servants/apprentices
rubrics_metrics.description: Masters should be wary what kind of Servants he keeps, and what kind of Apprentices he takes; look well to your shop, keep strict account of goods bought and sold; neglect emboldens servants to be bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice for employers: supervise closely, take strict inventories, and avoid negligent oversight that permits pilfering and corruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncleanness (sexual immorality) is filthy and reigning
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncleanness is a filthy sin and 'one of the most reigning sins in our day', spreading especially when great and chief set examples; it is 'beastly' and heavily condemned by scripture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat sexual immorality as widely dangerous and contagious, particularly when practised or modelled by the powerful; oppose and avoid it publicly and privately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the harlot's house ('Come not near the door of her house')
rubrics_metrics.description: The Wise man's counsel: 'Come not near the door of her house' — the harlot entices with sights, speech, perfumes, and 'decked' bed; proximity and familiarity are the path to ensnarement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical rule of avoidance: do not loiter near, enter, or seek out places of prostitution; remove oneself from tempting opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncleanness: poverty and bodily ruin (including the Pox)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncleanness often brings a man to want and poverty (a whore will not yield without hire) and brings diseases, notably the 'Foul Disease' (the Pox), which is nauseous, infectious, and visible shame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider both economic and bodily consequences as deterrents; understand specific disease-related punishments are associated with sexual sin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncleanness: social shame, murder of illegitimate children, and legal punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: This sin is attended with outward shame and disgrace; it is sometimes followed by murder of the babe begotten on the defiled bed, and historically actors have come to condign punishment (hanging, sudden death by fire from Heaven in tales cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise the severe social and legal consequences, including stories offered as moral examples; these are used to warn and shame potential transgressors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncleanness: spiritual ruin and no inheritance in Christ's kingdom
rubrics_metrics.description: Those common in this sin have 'none Inheritance in the Kingdom of Christ and of God' — it is a snare to the soul that, without a miracle of Grace, unavoidably perishes in the pleasures of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View sexual sin as jeopardising eternal salvation; emphasise the need for fear of God and reliance on grace to resist and recover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example of Joseph: steadfast refusal under temptation
rubrics_metrics.description: Joseph refused his mistress despite daily temptation, solicitation, provocation, contempt, slander, imprisonment, and danger of death; he 'hearkned not' and fled, leaving his garment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Joseph as a positive exemplar: resist temptation consistently, even at great cost; courageous refusal is the model behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of bad families and company: corruption by example
rubrics_metrics.description: Being put out of a godly family into a wicked one is a sign of God's anger; in bad families there are continual examples and incitements to evil and 'haunts and Walks of the infernal Spirits.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parents must ensure children are placed in godly households; those taking in children should be careful whom they receive to prevent moral contagion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divine judgments and exemplary punishments as deterrents
rubrics_metrics.description: The text recounts examples (instant death by fire, hanging, suicide from horror of conscience) and scriptural punishments to demonstrate God's indignation and to deter sinners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stories of severe divine or social punishment as moral instruction and deterrence; present narrative exemplars to warn audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypocrisy of masters: condemning in others what they allow in themselves
rubrics_metrics.description: Bad masters may condemn servants for sins that they themselves practise or permit; 'they condemn that in another which they either have, or do allow in themselves.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique hypocritical moralizing; call for consistency between a master's behaviour and the moral standards he enforces.
